framework.summary: The bill requires no safety framework or plan.

transparency_report.summary: The bill requires no public report or disclosure.

incident_reporting.summary: The bill requires no incident reporting.

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: The bill sets no imminent-risk reporting window.

third_party_audit.summary: The bill requires no audit or independent evaluation.

whistleblower.summary: The bill has no employee protections.

registration.summary: The bill requires no registration or licensing; it only conditions an antitrust exemption on notice to the Antitrust Division.

shutdown.summary: The bill requires no shutdown capability.

compute_threshold.summary: Coverage does not depend on training compute.

revenue_threshold.summary: Coverage does not depend on revenue, spending or users.

harm_threshold.summary: Covered risks are described by type, with no death, injury or damage figures.

penalties.summary: The Attorney General may seek an injunction against entities whose coordination violates antitrust law; no fines are set.
penalties.quote: The Attorney General may seek, in a court of competent jurisdiction, an injunction against the non-Federal entities

effective_date.summary: The bill text states no effective date.

notes: Antitrust-exemption bill, not a developer-duty bill. Entry names a Senate companion (S. 5105) whose text I did not read. Sec. 3(a)(2) requires written notice to the Assistant Attorney General before a coordinated delay, as a condition of the exemption; I did not count this as registration.
